# datarust

> Scikit-learn-style classical machine learning, preprocessing, and automated data profiling in Rust with zero external dependencies by default.

datarust is an ecosystem of independent, pure-Rust crates for machine learning and data science workloads. It features exact bit-level parity with scikit-learn estimators, high-performance scalers, encoders, imputers, pipelines, and automated data-quality profiling.

## Developer Resources & AI Endpoints

- [datarust Developer Portal](https://datarust.dev/developers/): Central developer hub indexing API docs, OpenAPI specs, MCP server, and SDK guides.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server](https://datarust.dev/docs/mcp/): Comprehensive documentation of the datarust MCP server endpoint (`https://datarust.dev/mcp`) and available tools.
- [MCP Server Card](https://datarust.dev/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json): Machine-readable SEP-1649 MCP server manifest declaring capabilities and tool metadata.
- [Smithery MCP Registry](https://smithery.ai/server/@genc-murat/datarust): Verified Smithery listing for automated Claude Desktop / Cursor installation.
- [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](https://datarust.dev/.well-known/ard.json): ARD v0.91 resource catalog indexing MCP servers, agent skills, and API docs.
- [Legacy AI Catalog](https://datarust.dev/.well-known/ai-catalog.json): Backward-compatible AI discovery manifest.
- [API Reference (docs.rs)](https://datarust.dev/docs/api/): Rust crate API documentation, structs, traits, and method signatures on docs.rs.
- [RFC 9727 API Catalog](https://datarust.dev/.well-known/api-catalog): Linkset catalog pointing to docs.rs and crate repository resources.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 Specification](https://datarust.dev/openapi.json): Complete OpenAPI schema with operationIds for machine learning and profiling endpoints.
- [Agent Skills](https://datarust.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): Discovery index for data-profiling and classical-ml agent skills.
- [DNS for AI Discovery (DNS-AID)](https://datarust.dev/docs/dns-aid/): DNS-based agent discovery records under `_agents.datarust.dev`.

## Core Documentation

- [Introduction](https://datarust.dev/docs/): Overview of datarust and datarust-profile crates.
- [Quick Start](https://datarust.dev/docs/quickstart/): Getting started guide with model fitting and evaluation.
- [Installation](https://datarust.dev/docs/installation/): Cargo dependency configurations and optional feature flags (`serde`, `rayon`, `matrixmultiply`, `datasets`).
- [Core Concepts](https://datarust.dev/docs/concepts/): Fundamental traits (`Estimator`, `Predictor`, `Transformer`, `Regressor`, `Classifier`, `Clusterer`).
- [datarust-profile Overview](https://datarust.dev/docs/profile/README/): Automated data profiling, quality checks, and report generation in Rust.
- [Performance vs scikit-learn](https://datarust.dev/docs/performance/): Benchmarks and latency comparisons.
- [Feature Comparison](https://datarust.dev/docs/comparison/): Feature matrix comparing datarust capabilities to scikit-learn.
- [Architecture](https://datarust.dev/docs/architecture/): Architecture notes on zero-dependency design and pure-Rust linear algebra solvers.

## Free Tier, Self-Serve Keys & Sandbox Access

- **Free Tier**: 100% free and open-source under the permissive MIT license.
- **Self-Serve Keys**: No API key, registration, or credit card required. All public endpoints, MCP tools, and REST APIs are immediately accessible.
- **Interactive Sandbox**: Instant developer and AI agent sandbox available via `https://datarust.dev/mcp` and browser demos at `https://datarust.dev/docs/quickstart/`.
- **Zero Onboarding Friction**: Autonomous AI agents and developers can make REST or MCP calls immediately without waiting for API key provisioning or registration.

## Agent Guidance: When to Use

- **When to use datarust**: Use when building machine learning pipelines, preprocessing datasets (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, OneHotEncoder, SimpleImputer), fitting linear regression, ridge, logistic regression, or k-means in native Rust without Python or C/Fortran runtime dependencies.
- **When to use datarust-profile**: Use when performing automated exploratory data analysis (EDA), generating data quality metrics, detecting target leakage, or outputting JSON/HTML profiling summaries.
- **When to use the MCP Server (`https://datarust.dev/mcp`)**: Use when an AI coding assistant (Cursor, Claude, Antigravity) needs to run remote data profiling, feature transformation, or model evaluation on tabular data.
